locator.section: 8.x Transition-state structure / ring size of the rearrangement (five- and six-membered transition states favored). Equation 8.20 branch (a), labelled 'rH'.

evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.20, FAVORED branch (a), labelled 'rH' (hydrogen rearrangement). 2-phenylethanol molecular ion loses formaldehyde (CH2=O) through a SIX-membered transition state (ring atoms O2-C1-C3-C4-C5 plus the migrating H8) to give the LESS-STABLE methylenecyclohexadiene radical cation (C7H8+., m/z 92). Text: 'The preference for a six-membered transition state also applies to the elimination of formaldehyde from 2-phenylethanol, which forms the less-stable (dHf = 0.3 eV) methylenecyclohexadiene ion (Equation 8.20, Burgers et al. 1982).' ARC COUNT (convention D): the page draws a DENSE concerted-radical depiction of roughly six fishhook (half-arrow) arcs threaded around the six-membered TS -- the O-H bond over to the ortho ring carbon, ring pi-bond shifts, the ipso->benzylic (exocyclic) pi formation, and the C1-C3/C1=O2 region -- together with a TRANSIENT distonic marking, a dot (.) drawn on the carbinol carbon C1 and a (+) drawn near the benzylic/ipso carbon inside the TS. Book draws ~6 fishhook arc(s); none is an implicit hook -- every bond-forming/breaking electron is drawn (6 single-electron fishhooks = the 3 encoded double-barbed 2e moves paired up). ENCODING: I encode the NET bond reorganization as a balanced 6-electron retro-ene-type (pericyclic) flow with three double-barbed (2e) moves: move<1> O2-H8 sigma -> new C5-H8 bond (H8 delivered to the ortho ring carbon C5); move<2> the C4=C5 ring pi -> the exocyclic C3=C4 pi; move<3> the C1-C3 sigma -> the new C1=O2 carbonyl pi (expelling neutral formaldehyde). CONVENTION C (delocalized aromatic radical cation): the aromatic ring radical cation is DELOCALIZED; the page draws +. on the ring in both the reactant and the product. I choose ONE localized Kekule/distonic resonance form -- odd electron on C9 (a meta-position carbon radical) and formal + on C10 (adjacent, allylic to the exocyclic methylene / benzylic-stabilized) -- consistently in precursor and both products, so the +. rides along as a SPECTATOR (no atom radical change, no radical arrow needed). The transient TS dot/plus that the book draws on C1/benzylic is the concerted midpoint, not an isolable species. CONVENTION F: no m/z and no % are printed for this ion on the page; observed_mz 92.0621 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C7H8+. from this instantiation, status 'inferred', detected=false, relative_intensity omitted.

No MØD rule is indexed to equation 8.20 (rule_index by_equation has no '8.20' key; the ch.8 index runs 8.1-8.14, and no 'entries' DFS is tagged 8.20). Nothing to cross-link. The related aromatic-loss family rules for other equations were not verified against this substrate; convention E cross-links are therefore not asserted here.
